newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures start lower but recover.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures start lower but recover.

text.p: CME lumber futures started slightly lower but found support in early trade from an oversold condition and turned higher early, traders said.
At 0929 CDT, lumber traded $2.00 to $0.70 higher with May up most at $399.50 per thousand board feet and July up $0.70 at $397.20 per tbf.

Trading activity remained light as the market awaited fresh direction from the cash lumber prices, but firmed on oversold status. Wholesalers were discounting wood to move stocks while mills were generally holding firm on asking prices, traders said.
